free_tier.stated: No free tier. 德国NAT-LXC is CNY 1.99 a month plus a one-off CNY 1.00 setup fee, printed '起价 ￥1.99 元 每月 + ￥1.00 初装费'. The page showed '5 可用' in stock.

retention.stated: monthly billing; no deletion interval after expiry was published on the pages read, and the vendor states '非我方问题拒绝退款' (no refund where the fault is not theirs)

egress.terms: unlimited traffic under fair use at 1 Gbps, printed '带宽：1 Gbps ，不限流量（合理使用）'
egress.free_allowance: unlimited under fair use, with no byte figure published

interface_detail: LXC guest on Alpine 3.20; the panel shows a private IP and a console, and the SSH port is computed from the last octet of the private IP
tooling: any SSH client; the vendor publishes a web port calculator at jsq.wuyoucloud.de so the mapping is scriptable
chaining: a 512 MB box at CNY 1.99 a month, the largest RAM of any sub-USD-0.50 row found, with a port-mapping rule simple enough to compute in a script

limits.value: 10 free ports per machine, derived from the private IP: SSH is 10000 plus the last octet and the free range is 20000 plus the last octet times 10, plus 0 to 9, so 10 ports
no byte allowance; unlimited under fair use, so the throttle is discretionary

binding_note: 10 computed ports is the whole inbound budget, and because they are derived from the private IP rather than chosen, the buyer cannot pick a well-known port such as 443.

identity_cost.detail: a WHMCS account; the registration form marks first name, last name and email as required, with phone, address, city, postcode and company present but not marked required, and no national ID field. Payment rails could not be read, because the cart requires login before it shows a payment method, so a card is inferred from the absence of a published rail rather than read. No ID document is requested at registration.

reliability_note: the group page states 'nat产品，共享v4 默认墙' (NAT products share IPv4 and are blocked by default) and '该机器不对任何运营数据做保证' (the machine carries no guarantee of any operating metric); no uptime figure or SLA published

notes: The best RAM-per-dollar row: 512 MB plus 100 MB of swap for CNY 1.99 a month, which is USD 0.2983 at the ECB reference rate of 6.6702 CNY per USD read, and it is in stock at 5 units. The 512 MB matters because it is twice what CrockyHost's entry plan gives for a third of the price, and it is the only sub-USD-0.30 row found that is not 256 MB. Three caveats. The setup fee of CNY 1.00 is charged once on top, so the first month is CNY 2.99 and every month after is CNY 1.99. The port mapping is computed rather than chosen: SSH is 10000 plus the last octet of the private IP and the free range is ten consecutive ports, so a well-known port cannot be selected, and the vendor's own header says the shared IPv4 is 'blocked by default'. And the vendor prints '该机器不对任何运营数据做保证', a blanket disclaimer of any operating guarantee, on the plan itself. No legal entity is named anywhere read, which is the same gap as the other two Chinese sellers. What is not established: the payment rails, because the cart needs a login; whether the ten ports carry UDP, which matters because a WireGuard endpoint needs one and nothing read says so; and whether the plan survives renewal at the same price. The vendor runs an Arabic, Persian, Turkish, Romanian and Ukrainian interface alongside Chinese, which suggests a deliberate non-Chinese customer base, but that is an inference from a language menu and not evidence about identity requirements.
